section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: riscos-prm locates entries in the online RISC OS Programmer's Reference Manuals. It accepts the name of a chapter, vector, command, service, or SWI and presents the matching documentation as a Markdown summary, a URL, or a page opened in a browser.

SWIs and services are summarised in the terminal by default. Other entries are opened in a browser or browser-like tool. When standard output is not a terminal, the URL is printed instead, making the command suitable for use by scripts and other tools.

subsection.title: Lookups
subsection.p: An unqualified lookup searches chapters, vectors, commands, services, and SWIs. The singular category switches restrict the search to one or more of those categories. SWIs and services may also be selected by hexadecimal number using the forms SWI number and Service number.

A SWI name followed by a reason number selects that reason, where the manual documents it separately. Names are matched without regard to case or spaces. The matching also allows for a leading * on command names and common differences involving the words "The", "module", and "RISC OS".

If a lookup has a single match, that entry is handled using the selected output mode. If several entries match, they are listed and the command exits with status 2. Multiple SWI or service matches can be rendered together when all of them support summaries.

subsection.title: Output modes
subsection.p: The default output mode summarises SWIs and services as Markdown. Other types are opened using a browser command. --url prints the manual URL, --open requests browser opening, and --summary requests the interface summary. The --no-tables switch replaces Markdown tables in a summary with a simpler representation.

subsection.title: Opening manual pages
subsection.p: The BROWSER environment variable selects the browser command. When it is unset or set to auto, riscos-prm tries host-open, w3m, links, and lynx, followed by open on macOS or xdg-open on other host systems.

subsection.title: Caching
subsection.p: The manual index and fetched pages are cached in the riscos-prm directory below XDG_CACHE_HOME. If that environment variable is not set, the cache is stored in ~/.cache/riscos-prm. Deleting the cached files causes them to be fetched again when next needed.

subsection.title: Exit status
subsection.p:
The command returns one of the following status values:
0 - a reference was found and handled.
1 - no reference was found.
2 - multiple references matched.
3 - no browser was available, or a summary could not be produced.

use.p: The command downloads the published manual index when it is not already cached, searches the selected categories, and handles the matching entry in the requested output mode. Quote a numeric lookup or a multi-word name when the shell would otherwise split it into separate arguments; unquoted name arguments are joined before matching.

SWIs and services are summarised by default. Other entries are opened with the browser selected by BROWSER, or by the first available browser command. The manual index and fetched pages are retained in the user's cache directory.

An exit status of 0 indicates a handled match. Status 1 means that nothing matched, status 2 means that several references matched, and status 3 means that no browser was available or the requested summary could not be produced.
